observations: A red and ochre upright figure with pointed ears occupies the center; two large circular eyes contain flower-like rings drawn in black outline over yellow fills.
Horizontal zigzag lines in black, yellow, and white cross the full width of the image at mid-height, layered over the blue-purple background wash.
Small rectangular marks and looping scribbles in orange, red, pink, and white are scattered across all four corners, sitting on top of broad blue brushed shapes.
reading: The figure holds its ground at center, arms raised, while the background pushes back with wide blue sweeps. Flower-ring eyes give the face an alert, almost wired quality. Zigzag bands cut across the body like interference, and the corner marks feel like static that never quite settles. The mood sits somewhere between confrontation and comedy, neither fully resolved.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #241 and nnxyz nnotb #243 share the same layered-line approach, but #242 swaps #241's warm ochre ground for a cool blue field. Title order and recorded creation order align for these three owned works.

connections.reason: Both #242 and #243 place a pointed-eared figure with paired circular eyes at center against a layered background, but #243 uses a dark body on warm yellow while #242 reverses to a red-ochre body on cool blue.

In #241 a spike-crown ring and a single spiral eye anchor a dark central form on warm ochre; #242 echoes the spike crown and ringed eyes but distributes them across a blue ground with a fuller upright body.

lookingQuestion: How do the horizontal zigzag bands relate to the figure's body — do they pass behind it, through it, or in front of it, and what does that layering do to the sense of space?
ambiguities: The flower-ring forms inside the eyes could be read as mechanical dials or organic rosettes; the image does not resolve which.
